issues.title: Create Joy App Splash Screen for Biner Labs
issues.description:
**Title:** Create Joy App Splash Screen for Biner Labs

**Description:**

Create a single splash screen for the Joy mobile app by Biner Labs, using one consistent visual design across iOS and Android. The screen should establish the Joy identity immediately through the Joy character, Joy app logo, and Biner Labs branding, while remaining simple and focused as the app’s opening screen. The Joy app is part of a physical AI personal-assistant product with a playful, friendly character identity. :contentReference[oaicite:0]{index=0}

**Design at:** https://www.figma.com/design/4M6ZJeHGYWaNO9bODM7Pou/Joy?node-id=21-171&t=gCSao4jUypxYHUIR-11

**Preferences:**https://www.figma.com/design/4M6ZJeHGYWaNO9bODM7Pou/Joy?node-id=21-173&t=gCSao4jUypxYHUIR-11

**Requirements:**
* Create one mobile splash-screen design that can be reused consistently across iOS and Android.
* Place the Joy character as the primary visual focus in the central area of the screen.
* Include the Joy app logo with clear visual prominence and sufficient separation from the character artwork.
* Include the Biner Labs logo or the copy “By Biner Labs” as secondary branding near the bottom of the screen.
* Keep the content hierarchy focused: Joy character first, Joy app identity second, and Biner Labs branding third.
* Use the existing Joy and Biner Labs brand assets, colors, typography, and visual style when available.
* Keep the composition playful, friendly, and character-driven without adding buttons, onboarding content, loading percentages, feature descriptions, or unrelated controls.
* Respect mobile safe areas and ensure the layout remains visually balanced across common iOS and Android screen proportions.
* Use Auto Layout where appropriate so the vertical spacing adapts cleanly between supported mobile frame sizes.
* Create clearly named layers and groups, including `Joy Character`, `Joy App Logo`, and `Biner Labs Branding`.
* Name the final frame `Splash Screen`.
* Do not create additional screens or prototype destinations; the requested scope is the splash screen only.

**Constraints (Do not change):**
* Use Lucide for icons, but use real company logos when needed.
* Follow the style referenced on the “Preferences” page in Figma.
* Reuse existing frames, components, typography, spacing, colors, and visual patterns when needed.

issues.title: Design the Joy Mobile Login Screen
issues.description:
**Title:** Design the Joy Mobile Login Screen

**Description:**

Create a new mobile login screen for the Joy app as the entry point to the authenticated experience. The screen should use Google SSO as the primary sign-in method and transition to the existing Home screen after successful authentication. Design one consistent layout that works for both iOS and Android, using the visual style, branding, typography, colors, spacing, and component patterns established on the Figma “Preferences” page. The Joy product specification defines Google SSO as the mobile authentication method and the Login screen as part of the AuthStack. :contentReference[oaicite:0]{index=0}

**Design at:** https://www.figma.com/design/4M6ZJeHGYWaNO9bODM7Pou/Joy?node-id=36-201&t=gCSao4jUypxYHUIR-11

**Preferences:** https://www.figma.com/design/4M6ZJeHGYWaNO9bODM7Pou/Joy?node-id=21-173&t=gCSao4jUypxYHUIR-11

**Components:** https://www.figma.com/design/4M6ZJeHGYWaNO9bODM7Pou/Joy?node-id=21-199&p=f&t=gCSao4jUypxYHUIR-11

* Create or reuse a reusable Google sign-in button component with default, pressed, loading, disabled, and error-recovery variants.
* Reuse existing brand, typography, button, surface, and feedback components from the current design library.
* Add any newly required reusable component to the **Components** page.

**Requirements:**

* Create a mobile frame named `Auth / Login`.
* Use a single layout structure for both iOS and Android, with platform-safe top and bottom areas.
* Follow the visual direction and design system defined on the Figma “Preferences” page.
* Present the Joy brand or character artwork as the primary visual element only when an approved asset or pattern already exists in the referenced design system.
* Establish a clear vertical hierarchy consisting of brand area, welcome message, supporting copy, Google sign-in action, and secondary legal copy.
* Use the heading copy `Welcome to Joy`.
* Use concise supporting copy that explains that signing in connects the user to their Joy device and settings.
* Use `Continue with Google` as the primary button label.
* Include the official Google logo inside the sign-in button.
* Keep the primary sign-in action visually prominent and reachable within the lower portion of the screen without conflicting with the device safe area.
* Include concise Terms of Service and Privacy Policy acknowledgement below the primary action, using existing link styling from the design system.
* Create a loading state where the Google sign-in button displays progress and cannot be pressed repeatedly.
* Create an authentication error state using the existing feedback pattern from the Preferences page, with clear recovery copy and a retry action.
* Create a temporary disabled state for the sign-in button when authentication cannot begin.
* Prototype the default Google sign-in button interaction to the loading state.
* Prototype successful authentication from the loading state to the existing Home screen using the transition pattern established in the Figma file.
* Prototype authentication failure from the loading state to the error state.
* Keep the screen focused on Google SSO and do not add email, password, guest login, account creation, or unrelated onboarding actions.
* Use Auto Layout for the full screen and all reusable content groups.
* Ensure text and controls maintain accessible contrast according to the referenced design system.
* Ensure the primary button has a minimum touch target of 44 × 44 px.
* Support Dynamic Type or equivalent text scaling without clipping or overlapping important controls.
* Provide a reduced-motion prototype variant when the referenced design uses animated transitions.
* Name related prototype frames `Auth / Login / Default`, `Auth / Login / Loading`, and `Auth / Login / Error`.

**Constraints (Do not change):**

* Use Lucide for icons, but use real company logos when needed.
* Follow the style referenced on the “Preferences” page in Figma.
* Reuse existing frames, components, typography, spacing, colors, and visual patterns when needed.
* The design must use the library. If a new library or component needs to be created, save it on the **Components** page.

issues.title: Create Joy Device Setup Flow and Connection States
issues.description:
**Title:** Create Joy Device Setup Flow and Connection States

**Description:**

Design the Joy device setup flow shown immediately after a new user completes Google authentication. The flow should help the user connect their physical Joy device before entering the main application, while preserving the typography, spacing, colors, illustration style, and bottom-aligned action pattern from the existing Auth / Login frames. Create multiple frames for the default, searching, device-found, connecting, error, and success states, with prototype transitions between each state.

**Design at:** https://www.figma.com/design/4M6ZJeHGYWaNO9bODM7Pou/Joy?node-id=36-338&p=f&t=gCSao4jUypxYHUIR-11

**Preferences:** https://www.figma.com/design/4M6ZJeHGYWaNO9bODM7Pou/Joy?node-id=21-28&p=f&t=gCSao4jUypxYHUIR-11

**Components:**  https://www.figma.com/design/4M6ZJeHGYWaNO9bODM7Pou/Joy?node-id=21-199&p=f&t=gCSao4jUypxYHUIR-11

* Reuse the existing Joy character illustration, typography styles, button styling, footer treatment, spacing system, and mobile frame dimensions from the Auth / Login designs.
* Reuse the existing primary button component and its default and loading variants.
* Create or update a reusable device status component with searching, found, connecting, connected, and error variants.
* Create a reusable Joy device card component for displaying the device illustration, name, and connection status.
* Create a reusable inline error message component that visually follows the existing authentication error treatment.

**Requirements:**

* Create a multi-state device setup flow using the following frame naming structure:
  * `Onboarding / Device Setup / Default`
  * `Onboarding / Device Setup / Searching`
  * `Onboarding / Device Setup / Device Found`
  * `Onboarding / Device Setup / Connecting`
  * `Onboarding / Device Setup / Error`
  * `Onboarding / Device Setup / Success`
* Place this flow after the existing `Auth / Login / Loading` frame when authentication succeeds and the user does not yet have a connected Joy device.
* Preserve the existing mobile frame size, white background, centered content hierarchy, generous vertical spacing, and bottom-aligned primary action pattern used on the login screen.
* Keep the setup method visually technology-agnostic. Do not mention or depict Bluetooth, Wi-Fi, QR codes, pairing codes, cables, or other connection methods that have not been defined.
* In `Onboarding / Device Setup / Default`:
  * Display the existing Joy character illustration near the upper-middle section of the screen.
  * Use the title `Let’s connect your Joy`.
  * Use the supporting copy `Connect your Joy device to manage its settings and integrations.`
  * Add a full-width primary button labeled `Set up Joy`.
  * Add a low-emphasis text action labeled `I’ll do this later` below the primary button.
  * Prototype `Set up Joy` to the Searching frame.
  * Prototype `I’ll do this later` to the existing Home frame when available; otherwise, connect it to a lightweight destination reference labeled `Home`.
* In `Onboarding / Device Setup / Searching`:
  * Keep the Joy illustration and primary content placement consistent with the default frame.
  * Use the title `Looking for your Joy…`.
  * Use the supporting copy `Keep your Joy nearby while we look for an available device.`
  * Show a visible but lightweight searching animation using component variants and Smart Animate.
  * Replace the primary action with a loading button labeled `Searching…`.
  * Include a secondary text action labeled `Cancel` that returns to the Default frame.
  * Prototype the successful search state to `Device Found`.
  * Prototype a failed or timed-out search to the Error frame.
* In `Onboarding / Device Setup / Device Found`:
  * Use the title `Joy found!`.
  * Use the supporting copy `This Joy is ready to connect to your account.`
  * Display a device card containing the Joy illustration, device name `Joy`, and status label `Ready to connect`.
  * Add a primary button labeled `Connect Joy`.
  * Add a secondary text action labeled `Search again`.
  * Prototype `Connect Joy` to the Connecting frame.
  * Prototype `Search again` to the Searching frame.
* In `Onboarding / Device Setup / Connecting`:
  * Use the title `Connecting to Joy…`.
  * Use the supporting copy `This should only take a moment.`
  * Display the same device card with its status changed to `Connecting`.
  * Use a loading variant of the primary button labeled `Connecting…`.
  * Prevent additional actions while the connection is in progress.
  * Use a subtle looping animation on the device status indicator rather than introducing a new full-screen visual style.
  * Prototype successful completion to the Success frame and unsuccessful completion to the Error frame.
* In `Onboarding / Device Setup / Error`:
  * Use the title `Joy could not connect`.
  * Use the supporting copy `Make sure your Joy is ready, then try again.`
  * Display the device card with an error status labeled `Connection failed`.
  * Include an inline error message using the same visual language as the existing authentication error state.
  * Add a primary button labeled `Try again`.
  * Add a secondary text action labeled `Back`.
  * Prototype `Try again` to the Connecting frame.
  * Prototype `Back` to the Default frame.
* In `Onboarding / Device Setup / Success`:
  * Use a cheerful Joy illustration or expression consistent with the existing character asset.
  * Use the title `Joy is ready!`.
  * Use the supporting copy `Your Joy is connected and ready to use.`
  * Display the device card with the device name `Joy` and a success status labeled `Connected`.
  * Add a primary button labeled `Go to Home`.
  * Prototype `Go to Home` to the existing Home frame when available; otherwise, connect it to a lightweight destination reference labeled `Home`.
* Use component variants rather than duplicate frames for local button states, status indicators, and device-card status changes.
* Use separate frames for the six full-screen states because the title, messaging, available actions, or overall interaction state changes materially.
* Use Auto Layout for the full screen, text groups, device card, error message, and bottom action area.
* Maintain safe-area spacing and ensure the primary action remains accessible on common mobile screen heights without overlapping system navigation areas.
* Keep all body copy readable at accessible contrast levels and avoid relying only on color to communicate connected or error states.
* Provide a reduced-motion prototype option where looping searching and connecting animations are replaced by static progress indicators.
* Use Smart Animate with subtle opacity and position changes between related setup states, avoiding dramatic transitions that conflict with the restrained Auth / Login visual style.
* Do not modify or redesign the existing Auth / Login frames as part of this task.

**Constraints (Do not change):**

* Use Lucide for icons, but use real company logos when needed.
* Follow the style referenced on the “Preferences” page in Figma.
* Reuse existing frames, components, typography, spacing, colors, and visual patterns when needed.
* The design must use the library. If a new library or component needs to be created, save it on the **Components** page.

issues.title: Design Joy Home Dashboard Screen States
issues.description:
**Title:** Design Joy Home Dashboard Screen States

**Description:**

Design the main Joy Home Dashboard that users reach after authentication and the Joy pairing flow. The dashboard should clearly communicate device connection status, current voice activity, Spotify status, WhatsApp status, and access to Joy Settings while preserving the visual language already established on the Mobile page. This task requires multiple full-screen states for connected, unpaired, offline, and loading conditions, plus reusable component variants for local device and integration states.

**Design at:** https://www.figma.com/design/4M6ZJeHGYWaNO9bODM7Pou/Joy?node-id=36-338&p=f&t=gCSao4jUypxYHUIR-11

**Preferences:** https://www.figma.com/design/4M6ZJeHGYWaNO9bODM7Pou/Joy?node-id=21-28&p=f&t=gCSao4jUypxYHUIR-11

**Components:** https://www.figma.com/design/4M6ZJeHGYWaNO9bODM7Pou/Joy?node-id=21-199&p=f&t=gCSao4jUypxYHUIR-11

* Reuse `Component / Joy Character`.
* Reuse `Component / Button / Primary`.
* Reuse or extend `Component / Device Summary Card`.
* Reuse `Component / Status Message` where an inline warning or error message is needed.
* Reuse the existing typography, spacing, colors, rounded shapes, and 390 × 874 mobile frame patterns from the authentication and pairing flows.
* Create a reusable `Component / Joy Device Card` with variants for `Idle`, `Thinking`, `Speaking`, `Error`, and `Offline`.
* Create a reusable `Component / Integration Status Card` with variants for `Connected`, `Not Connected`, `Disabled`, and `Error`.
* Create reusable loading skeleton variants for the device card and integration cards.
* Save any new components and variants on the **Components** page.

**Requirements:**

* Create the following four full-screen frames:
  * `App / Home / Connected`
  * `App / Home / Not Connected`
  * `App / Home / Device Offline`
  * `App / Home / Loading`

* Use the existing `App / Home Screen` frame area as the destination for the new dashboard designs rather than creating an unrelated duplicate section.

* Design all frames at 390 × 874 and respect mobile safe areas.

* Use approximately 24 px horizontal page padding and follow the vertical spacing rhythm already established in the pairing flow.

* Keep the page background white and use the existing dark primary color, Joy turquoise accent, neutral grays, and established error color from the current Mobile designs.

* Add a compact top header containing:
  * Page title: `Home`
  * A settings icon action on the right
  * The settings action should prototype to the existing `App / Joy Settings` frame.

* For `App / Home / Connected`:
  * Treat this as the primary default Home Dashboard.
  * Place the reusable Joy Device Card as the most visually prominent element near the top of the content.
  * Show the Joy character artwork inside the device card.
  * Use sample device name: `Joy-8492-X1`.
  * Show a turquoise connection indicator with label: `Online`.
  * Show voice-state copy:
    * Status label: `Idle`
    * Supporting copy: `Joy is ready to listen.`
  * Include a secondary text action or card action labeled `Manage Joy`.
  * Prototype `Manage Joy` and tapping the device card to the existing `App / Joy Settings` frame.
  * Add a section heading below the device card: `Connections`.
  * Add a Spotify status card containing:
    * Real Spotify logo
    * Title: `Spotify`
    * Status: `Not connected`
    * Action: `Connect`
  * Add a WhatsApp status card containing:
    * Real WhatsApp logo
    * Title: `WhatsApp`
    * Status: `Not connected`
    * Action: `Set up`
  * Do not design the complete Spotify or WhatsApp setup flows in this task.
  * Add lightweight prototype destination references for the Spotify and WhatsApp actions without creating unrelated full screens.

* For `App / Home / Not Connected`:
  * Use this frame when the user selects `Connect Later` during onboarding.
  * Keep the same header and overall Home layout.
  * Replace the connected device card with an unpaired empty-state card.
  * Show the Joy character artwork prominently.
  * Use heading: `Connect your Joy`
  * Use supporting copy: `Pair a Joy to use voice controls and manage your device from the app.`
  * Add a primary action labeled `Connect Joy`.
  * Prototype `Connect Joy` to the existing `Onboarding / Joy Code / Empty` frame.
  * Keep the `Connections` section visible below the empty state.
  * Display Spotify and WhatsApp cards using the `Disabled` variant.
  * Add supporting text to disabled integration cards: `Connect a Joy first`.
  * Do not make disabled integration cards interactive.

* For `App / Home / Device Offline`:
  * Preserve the same hierarchy and content placement as the connected frame.
  * Change the Joy Device Card to the `Offline` variant.
  * Use a neutral gray connection indicator and label: `Offline`.
  * Use supporting copy: `Joy is offline. Check that it is powered on and connected to Wi-Fi.`
  * Add a visible action labeled `Open Joy Settings`.
  * Prototype the action to the existing `App / Joy Settings` frame.
  * Keep Spotify and WhatsApp status cards visible.
  * Clearly disable any voice-related interaction without removing the connection information.
  * Do not rely only on color to communicate the offline state.

* For `App / Home / Loading`:
  * Preserve the final dashboard layout so content does not shift dramatically after loading.
  * Replace the device card content, device labels, and integration card content with subtle skeleton placeholders.
  * Keep the top header visible.
  * Avoid using a full-page blocking spinner.
  * Use a restrained shimmer or opacity animation that matches the clean visual style of the existing app.

* Create the following local variants for `Component / Joy Device Card`:
  * `State=Idle`
    * Turquoise online indicator
    * Label: `Idle`
    * Copy: `Joy is ready to listen.`
  * `State=Thinking`
    * Label: `Thinking`
    * Copy: `Joy is working on your request.`
    * Add a subtle animated dots or pulsing indicator.
  * `State=Speaking`
    * Label: `Speaking`
    * Copy: `Joy is responding.`
    * Add a compact animated sound-wave or voice indicator.
  * `State=Error`
    * Error status styling using the established red color.
    * Label: `Something went wrong`
    * Copy: `Joy could not complete the last request.`
  * `State=Offline`
    * Neutral gray styling.
    * Label: `Offline`
    * Include the offline explanation and settings action.

* Use component variants for voice-state changes instead of creating separate full Home frames for `Idle`, `Thinking`, `Speaking`, and `Error`.

* Create the following local variants for `Component / Integration Status Card`:
  * `Status=Connected`
  * `Status=Not Connected`
  * `Status=Disabled`
  * `Status=Error`

* The `Connected` integration variant should support:
  * Service logo
  * Service name
  * Short connected-account or connection label
  * A subtle success indicator
  * A trailing chevron or management action

* The `Not Connected` integration variant should support:
  * Service logo
  * Service name
  * `Not connected` status
  * A clear setup action

* The `Disabled` integration variant should:
  * Reduce emphasis without making text unreadable.
  * Explain why the action is unavailable.
  * Avoid presenting the card as tappable.

* The `Error` integration variant should:
  * Show a concise inline error state.
  * Use the established error color.
  * Provide space for a `Retry` or `Review` action without designing the destination flow.

* Connect the existing pairing flow to the new Home frames:
  * `Onboarding / Joy Code / Success` → `App / Home / Connected` when `Continue to Home` is selected.
  * `Onboarding / Joy Code / Skip Sheet Overlay` → `App / Home / Not Connected` when `Connect Later` is selected.
  * `Continue Pairing` should continue dismissing the skip confirmation overlay and return to the pairing screen.

* Use Smart Animate for transitions between Joy Device Card voice-state variants.
  * Duration: approximately 200–300 ms.
  * Use subtle ease-out motion.
  * Avoid large movement or playful animation that distracts from status clarity.

* Use a simple dissolve or short slide transition when navigating from pairing success to Home.

* Provide a reduced-motion prototype behavior using dissolve transitions and static state indicators instead of pulsing, shimmer, or sound-wave animations.

* Maintain a clear hierarchy:
  * Header
  * Primary Joy device status
  * Device action
  * Connections section
  * Spotify and WhatsApp status cards

* Keep important status text readable at a glance and avoid placing critical information only inside icons.

* Ensure all interactive targets are at least 44 × 44 px.

* Maintain sufficient contrast for text, status indicators, disabled content, and error messages.

* Use Auto Layout for the page content, device card, integration card stack, and reusable internal component groups.

* Name layers semantically, including:
  * `Header`
  * `Joy Device Card`
  * `Device Identity`
  * `Voice Status`
  * `Connections Section`
  * `Spotify Status Card`
  * `WhatsApp Status Card`
  * `Primary Action`
  * `Loading Skeleton`

* Do not add recent activity, chat history, manual remote controls, media playback controls, notification feeds, or unrelated dashboard widgets in this task.

**Constraints (Do not change):**

* Use Lucide for icons, but use real company logos when needed.
* Follow the style referenced on the “Preferences” page in Figma.
* Reuse existing frames, components, typography, spacing, colors, and visual patterns when needed.
* The design must use the library. If a new library or component needs to be created, save it on the **Components** page.

issues.title: Design Joy Settings and Personalization Flow
issues.description:
**Title:** Design Joy Settings and Personalization Flow

**Description:**


Design and expand the existing Joy mobile Settings experience into a complete personalization flow where users can manage their profile, paired Joy device, Joy speaking personality, voice and audio preferences, connected services, notifications, and app information. Reuse the current `App / Joy Settings` frame and surrounding Joy mobile screens as the visual source of truth, preserving the existing clean card-based layout, typography, spacing, bottom navigation, and monochrome visual hierarchy. The scope requires a main Settings frame, supporting detail frames, reusable local component variants, confirmation overlays, and prototype connections between all settings destinations.

**Design at:** Make it the photo profile use the real picture, and please remove the fill of the text who have the white fill.
**Preferences:** https://www.figma.com/design/4M6ZJeHGYWaNO9bODM7Pou/Joy?node-id=21-28&p=f&t=YBk4ut09pjdHfa4K-11

**Components:** https://www.figma.com/design/4M6ZJeHGYWaNO9bODM7Pou/Joy?node-id=21-199&p=f&t=YBk4ut09pjdHfa4K-11

* Reuse the existing bottom navigation bar, settings section container, grouped settings card, settings row, divider, chevron, status text, buttons, input fields, avatars, badges, and modal patterns available in the file.
* Update the reusable settings row to support optional leading icons or avatars, title, supporting text, status text, chevron, toggle, and destructive styling.
* Create reusable segmented-control or selection-card variants for Joy personality and response-length options.
* Create slider or stepper components for volume, speaking speed, and playfulness controls when no suitable library component already exists.
* Create reusable button variants for default, disabled, loading, destructive, and voice-preview playback states.
* Create reusable confirmation dialog variants for logging out and unpairing Joy.

**Requirements:**

* Create a multi-frame settings and personalization flow rather than a single static screen.
* Update the existing main frame and name it `Settings / Main`.
* Preserve the current mobile frame size, safe areas, bottom navigation, background color, section spacing, grouped-card styling, border treatment, typography hierarchy, and overall visual density used by the existing Home and Settings screens.
* Keep `Settings` selected in the bottom navigation on the main Settings frame.
* Use the following main page heading and supporting copy:
  * Title: `Settings`
  * Supporting copy: `Manage your account, Joy, connections, and preferences.`
* Organize `Settings / Main` into the following sections and rows:

  * `Account`
    * `Account & Profile`
    * Supporting text: the user’s display name or email
    * Display the user avatar as the leading visual element.

  * `My Joy`
    * `Joy Device`
    * Supporting text: `Online`, `Offline`, or `Not paired`
    * `Joy Personality`
    * Supporting text: selected preset, such as `Balanced`
    * `Voice & Audio`
    * Supporting text: `Default Joy voice`

  * `Connections`
    * `Spotify`
    * Supporting text: `Connected` or `Not connected`
    * Use the real Spotify logo.
    * `WhatsApp`
    * Supporting text: `Connected` or `Not connected`
    * Use the real WhatsApp logo.

  * `App Preferences`
    * `Notifications`
    * Supporting text: `Enabled` or `Disabled`
    * `Appearance`
    * Supporting text: selected appearance mode, such as `System`
    * `About & Version`
    * Supporting text: `v1.0.0`

* Keep `Log Out` as a separate destructive text action below the grouped sections rather than mixing it into a standard settings card.
* Ensure the main page remains vertically scrollable when content exceeds the available viewport while keeping the bottom navigation fixed.

* Create a frame named `Settings / Account & Profile`.
* Use a standard subpage navigation header with a back button and the title `Account & Profile`.
* Include a profile image area with an edit-photo affordance.
* Include editable fields for:
  * `Display name`
  * `Email`
* Present the email as read-only when it is tied to the user’s Google account.
* Include supporting text beneath the email field:
  * `Managed through your Google Account`
* Add a primary action labeled `Save Changes`.
* Use input component variants for default, focused, filled, validation error, and disabled states.
* Keep `Save Changes` disabled until the user modifies an editable value.
* Create button variants for disabled, enabled, and saving states.
* Add a secondary row or text action labeled `Manage Google Account`.
* Add a destructive text action labeled `Delete Account` at the bottom, visually separated from normal profile settings.
* Connect the back button to `Settings / Main`.
* Connect a successful save interaction back to the same frame with a lightweight success feedback state, such as a temporary inline confirmation reading `Profile updated`.

* Create a frame named `Settings / Joy Personality`.
* Use a subpage header with a back button and the title `Joy Personality`.
* Add supporting copy:
  * `Choose how Joy speaks while keeping Joy’s friendly personality.`
* Include a single-select preset section using large selection cards with the following exact options:

  * `Balanced`
    * Supporting copy: `The default Joy personality.`

  * `Playful`
    * Supporting copy: `More cheerful, expressive, and energetic.`

  * `Gentle`
    * Supporting copy: `Calmer, softer, and more reassuring.`

  * `Concise`
    * Supporting copy: `Short and direct responses.`

* Make `Balanced` selected by default in the primary frame.
* Use component variants for unselected, pressed, and selected personality cards rather than creating duplicate full-screen frames.
* Add a `Response Length` setting with a segmented control containing:
  * `Short`
  * `Balanced`
  * `Detailed`
* Add a `Playfulness` control with clearly labeled positions:
  * `Low`
  * `Default`
  * `High`
* Do not provide a freeform system-prompt or custom-instruction field.
* Keep the Joy output language fixed and do not add a language selector.
* Include a primary button labeled `Save Personality`.
* Keep the button disabled until a value changes.
* After saving, show a lightweight success state reading:
  * `Joy personality updated`
* Connect the back button and successful save action to `Settings / Main`.
* Update the supporting text shown on the `Joy Personality` row in `Settings / Main` to reflect the selected preset.

* Create a frame named `Settings / Voice & Audio`.
* Use a subpage header with a back button and the title `Voice & Audio`.
* Include a grouped section titled `Joy Voice`.
* Include a read-only voice row:
  * Title: `Voice`
  * Supporting text: `Joy Voice · Default`
* Include a prominent preview card with a button labeled `Play Test Voice`.
* Use local button variants for:
  * default;
  * playing;
  * completed;
  * unavailable.
* During the playing state, change the button label to `Playing…` and display a simple audio-progress or animated waveform treatment using component variants and Smart Animate.
* Add a `Joy Volume` control with the current percentage displayed.
* Add a `Speaking Speed` control with conservative labeled values:
  * `Slower`
  * `Normal`
  * `Faster`
* Keep `Normal` selected by default.
* Make it visually clear that these controls affect Joy’s spoken responses, not Spotify playback.
* Add a primary action labeled `Save Audio Settings`.
* Keep the action disabled until a value changes.
* Connect the back button and successful save action to `Settings / Main`.

* Create a frame named `Settings / Joy Device`.
* Use a subpage header with a back button and the title `Joy Device`.
* Display a device summary card containing:
  * Joy avatar;
  * device name `My Joy`;

issues.description:
**Title:** Design Joy Mobile Chat and Voice Conversation Flow

**Description:**

Design the primary Chat experience for the Joy mobile app, allowing users to interact with Joy through typed messages or recorded voice input within the same conversation. This screen acts as the mobile interface for the Joy assistant and should feel consistent with the existing Joy onboarding, Home, Settings, typography, colors, spacing, navigation, and visual personality. The scope includes the default chat screen, active conversation, voice recording, Joy thinking, response playback, failed-message recovery, empty conversation, and offline states using a combination of full-screen frames and reusable component variants.
Warna background color dari send message icon yang di halaman chat itu ketika text field-nya nggak aktif, seperti di halaman komposisi fokus, dijadikan background-nya. Jangan warna hitam gitu deh, kayak abu-abu aja gitu biar kesannya non clickable. Jadi, yang clickable itu yang ada di chat komposisi fokus saja, di mana clickable kalau memang ada teksnya di text field tersebut.
**Design at:**  https://www.figma.com/design/4M6ZJeHGYWaNO9bODM7Pou/Joy?node-id=0-1&p=f&t=YBk4ut09pjdHfa4K-11

**Preferences:** https://www.figma.com/design/4M6ZJeHGYWaNO9bODM7Pou/Joy?node-id=21-28&p=f&t=YBk4ut09pjdHfa4K-11

**Components:** https://www.figma.com/design/4M6ZJeHGYWaNO9bODM7Pou/Joy?node-id=21-199&p=f&t=YBk4ut09pjdHfa4K-11

* Reuse the existing mobile screen shell, safe-area treatment, bottom navigation, buttons, typography, colors, icons, cards, banners, and Joy character assets from the current Joy design.
* Create a reusable chat message component with variants for user text, user voice, Joy response, sending, failed, and retry states.
* Create a reusable message composer with variants for empty, focused, filled, disabled, and sending states.
* Create a reusable voice recorder component with variants for recording, paused, ready to send, and cancelled states.
* Create a reusable audio playback control with variants for idle, playing, paused, completed, and unavailable states.
* Create reusable system-status components for thinking, offline, reconnecting, and general conversation errors.
* Update the existing bottom navigation component to support `Home`, `Chat`, and `Settings`, with a clear active-state variant for `Chat`.

**Requirements:**

* Create a multi-state Chat flow for the Joy mobile app rather than a single static frame.
* Use a mobile frame size and safe-area behavior consistent with the existing Joy application screens.
* Keep the existing Joy visual language intact, including the light interface, soft pink accents, rounded components, friendly character illustration style, spacing rhythm, typography hierarchy, and bottom navigation behavior.
* Do not redesign the existing Home or Settings screens beyond updating the shared bottom navigation to include `Home`, `Chat`, and `Settings`.
* Position `Chat` as the center item in the bottom navigation and show it as active on all Chat frames.
* Use the screen title `Chat with Joy`.
* Add a compact supporting subtitle below the title: `Type or talk to Joy anytime.`
* Include a subtle Joy status indicator in the header area, using states such as `Online`, `Thinking`, and `Offline`.
* Keep the main conversation area vertically scrollable and visually dominant.
* Keep the message composer fixed above the bottom navigation and mobile safe area.
* The message composer must include:
  * Placeholder text: `Message Joy`
  * A microphone action for starting voice input
  * A send action that becomes active only after text is entered
  * Clear focused, filled, disabled, and sending variants
* Use Lucide icons for microphone, send, stop, play, pause, retry, close, and connectivity status.
* User messages should be visually aligned to the right.
* Joy messages should be visually aligned to the left and include a small Joy avatar or character marker.
* Keep message bubbles readable, compact, and visually distinct without using excessive borders or decorative effects.
* Add subtle metadata only when useful, such as `Voice message`, message time, delivery failure, or input source.
* Do not create separate Talk and Chat tabs. Voice input must exist inside the Chat experience as an alternative input method.

* Create the frame `Chat / Empty`:
  * Show the initial state before the user has sent a message.
  * Use a centered Joy illustration or avatar in the conversation area.
  * Display the heading `Hi! What should we talk about?`
  * Display the supporting copy `You can type a message or use your voice.`
  * Keep the composer available at the bottom.
  * Avoid filling the empty state with suggested prompts unless an existing Joy pattern already provides them.

* Create the frame `Chat / Active Conversation`:
  * Show a realistic mixed conversation containing both typed and voice messages.
  * Include at least one typed user message.
  * Include at least one user voice-message bubble with duration.
  * Include at least one Joy text response with an audio playback control.
  * Use concise English responses for Joy.
  * Example conversation content:
    * User: `What are we working on today?`
    * Joy: `Today we are designing the mobile chat experience. Joy is ready to help!`
    * User voice message duration: `0:08`
  * Show the composer in its default empty state after the latest response.

* Create the frame `Chat / Composer Focused`:
  * Show the mobile keyboard area only if it matches the presentation style used elsewhere in the referenced design.
  * Show the composer with entered text: `Can you explain that again?`
  * Show the send action in its active state.
  * Connect the send action to `Chat / Thinking`.

* Create the frame `Chat / Voice Recording`:
  * Replace or expand the normal composer into a clear recording interface.
  * Display a live recording timer such as `00:06`.
  * Include a simple animated waveform or pulsing audio indicator.
  * Display the label `Listening…`
  * Include a cancel action and a stop or finish-recording action.
  * Keep the rest of the conversation visible but visually de-emphasized.
  * Use a component variant for the pulsing or waveform animation and Smart Animate for the transition.
  * Connect the microphone action from the default composer to this frame.

* Create the frame `Chat / Voice Ready to Send`:
  * Show the completed recording as a compact preview before submission.
  * Include playback, duration, delete, and send controls.
  * Use the copy `Voice message ready`.
  * Allow the user to return to the normal composer by deleting or cancelling the recording.
  * Connect the send action to `Chat / Thinking`.

* Create the frame `Chat / Thinking`:
  * Add the submitted user message to the conversation.
  * Show a Joy response placeholder with the label `Joy is thinking…`
  * Use a subtle animated three-dot or character-thinking component.
  * Disable duplicate submission while the current response is being prepared.
  * Keep the user able to scroll through previous messages.
  * Use Smart Animate between the submitted message and the thinking response.
  * Connect the completed thinking state to `Chat / Response Received`.

* Create the frame `Chat / Response Received`:
  * Replace the thinking indicator with a completed Joy response.
  * Display the response as readable text.
  * Include a compact audio control inside or directly below the Joy response.
  * Show play and pause as component variants rather than duplicate full-screen frames.
  * Use the example response: `Sure! Joy means the mobile app will let you type or speak in the same conversation.`
  * Keep the composer available for the next message.

* Create the frame `Chat / Message Failed`:
  * Show the user message remaining in the conversation with a clear failure treatment.
  * Display the text `Message not sent`.
  * Include a `Retry` action and a secondary delete or dismiss action.
  * Do not remove the user’s typed text or voice message automatically.
  * Use an inline error treatment rather than a disruptive full-screen modal.
  * Connect `Retry` back to `Chat / Thinking`.

* Create the frame `Chat / Response Error`:
  * Keep the user message visible.
  * Replace the Joy thinking state with a friendly inline error card.
  * Use the copy:
    * Heading: `Joy could not answer`
    * Supporting text: `Please try again in a moment.`
    * Action: `Try Again`
  * Connect `Try Again` back to `Chat / Thinking`.

* Create the frame `Chat / Offline`:
  * Preserve the existing conversation history.
  * Show a persistent but compact offline banner near the top of the conversation area.
  * Use the copy:
    * Heading: `Joy is offline`
    * Supporting text: `Messages cannot be sent until the connection returns.`
  * Disable the send and microphone actions.
  * Keep entered draft text visible rather than clearing it.
  * Include a visual `Reconnecting…` status variant.
  * Avoid using color alone to communicate the offline state.

* Create the frame `Chat / Reconnected`:
  * Remove the offline banner.
  * Show a temporary success toast or status message: `Joy is back online.`
  * Restore the send and microphone actions.
  * Use a short dissolve or Smart Animate transition from the offline state.

* Create the audio playback component variants:
  * `Audio Reply / Idle`
  * `Audio Reply / Playing`
  * `Audio Reply / Paused`
  * `Audio Reply / Completed`
  * `Audio Reply / Unavailable`
  * Include play or pause control, elapsed time, total duration, and a simple progress indicator.
  * Keep the control compact enough to remain visually secondary to the message text.

* Create the message bubble component variants:
  * `Message / User Text`
  * `Message / User Voice`
  * `Message / User Sending`
  * `Message / User Failed`
  * `Message / Joy Text`
  * `Message / Joy Thinking`
  * `Message / Joy Error`
  * Ensure long text wraps correctly and bubbles respond gracefully to different message lengths.

* Create the composer component variants:
  * `Composer / Empty`
  * `Composer / Focused`
  * `Composer / Filled`
  * `Composer / Sending`
  * `Composer / Disabled`
  * Ensure all touch targets remain comfortably tappable and visually distinct.

* Prototype the primary interaction path:
  * `Chat / Empty` → tap text field → `Chat / Composer Focused`
  * `Chat / Composer Focused` → tap send → `Chat / Thinking`
  * `Chat / Empty` or `Chat / Active Conversation` → tap microphone → `Chat / Voice Recording`
  * `Chat / Voice Recording` → finish recording → `Chat / Voice Ready to Send`
  * `Chat / Voice Ready to Send` → tap send → `Chat / Thinking`
  * `Chat / Thinking` → timed transition → `Chat / Response Received`
  * `Chat / Message Failed` → tap retry → `Chat / Thinking`
  * `Chat / Offline` → connection restored → `Chat / Reconnected`
* Use Smart Animate for composer expansion, voice recording transitions, thinking animation, message insertion, and status changes.
* Use short, restrained animation timing so the interface feels responsive rather than theatrical.
* Include reduced-motion alternatives using simple dissolve transitions.
* Ensure text, icons, controls, status indicators, message bubbles, and disabled states meet accessible contrast requirements.
* Do not rely only on green, red, or other colors to communicate online, error, playing, or failed states.
* Keep touch targets at least 44 × 44 px where possible.
* Name frames, layers, components, and variants consistently using the naming patterns specified above.
* Place all newly created reusable components and variants on the existing **Components** page.
* Connect the `Home`, `Chat`, and `Settings` bottom navigation items to the existing destination frames where those frames already exist.

**Constraints (Do not change):**
* Use Lucide for icons, but use real company logos when needed.
* Follow the style referenced on the “Preferences” page in Figma.
* Reuse existing frames, components, typography, spacing, colors, and visual patterns when needed.
* The design must use the library. If a new library or component needs to be created, save it on the **Components** page.
* Create and validate each design frame one at a time. After completing a frame or component, take a screenshot and carefully review its layout, visual consistency, alignment, spacing, and overall quality. If anything looks incorrect or unpolished, revise the frame and repeat the validation process until it meets the expected quality. Only proceed to the next frame once the current frame or component has been fully validated.
* Use inline agent

## Tujuan

Melakukan slicing dan implementasi setiap komponen dari desain Figma secara **pixel-perfect** sebagai reusable component, kemudian menempatkannya berdasarkan cakupan penggunaan:

* **Global**: digunakan pada berbagai fitur atau screen.
* **Feature**: digunakan pada beberapa screen dalam satu fitur.
* **Local Screen**: hanya digunakan pada satu screen tertentu.

Penentuan scope wajib mengikuti panduan:

https://biner-labs.gitbook.io/biner-labs/engineering-guidelines-and-standards/reusable-component-scope

## Pengerjaan

1. Pelajari panduan **Reusable Component Scope** sebelum menentukan lokasi komponen.
2. Periksa codebase untuk memastikan komponen yang sama atau setara belum tersedia.
3. Gunakan **Figma Native MCP** untuk membaca struktur layer, ukuran, warna, typography, spacing, icon, asset, state, variant, dan properti layout.
4. Kerjakan link tersebut secara paralel menggunakan **spawn subagents / multiple agents**:

   * Satu subagent hanya menangani satu link Figma.
   * Setiap subagent wajib memeriksa komponen yang sudah tersedia di codebase.
   * Setiap subagent menentukan scope komponen sebagai `Global`, `Feature`, atau `Local Screen` beserta alasan singkatnya.
   * Implementasikan komponen hanya jika komponen yang sama atau setara belum tersedia.
5. Setelah seluruh subagent selesai, validasi hasil implementasi terhadap desain Figma dan panduan Reusable Component Scope.
6. Perbaiki ketidaksesuaian sampai tampilan akurat, scope tepat, dan tidak terdapat komponen duplikat.

## Requirements

* Implementasi harus mengikuti desain Figma secara akurat, termasuk:

  * Struktur dan hierarchy
  * Ukuran dan spacing
  * Warna dan typography
  * Border dan radius
  * Icon atau asset
  * State dan variant
  * Perilaku layout
* Scope ditentukan berdasarkan penggunaan komponen di dalam aplikasi, bukan hanya berdasarkan lokasi atau nama komponen di Figma.
* Gunakan kembali komponen yang sudah tersedia apabila fungsi dan tampilannya sama atau setara.

## Constraints

* Jangan membuat atau menduplikasi komponen yang sudah tersedia di codebase.
* Jangan menentukan scope berdasarkan asumsi atau sekadar potensi penggunaan kembali.
* Jangan menempatkan komponen sebagai `Global` kecuali memenuhi kriteria dalam panduan.
* Jangan mengubah screen atau bagian lain di luar komponen yang sedang dikerjakan.
* Jangan memberikan lebih dari satu link Figma kepada satu subagent.
* Jangan menyatakan pekerjaan selesai sebelum seluruh komponen divalidasi.

## Laporan Akhir

Sertakan:

* Nama komponen yang dibuat.
* Scope dan alasan pemilihannya.
* Lokasi file komponen.
* Komponen yang digunakan kembali beserta lokasi filenya.
* Hasil validasi terhadap desain Figma.
* Hasil validasi terhadap panduan Reusable Component Scope.
